commons:183258889.summary: Against a field of gold, Christ stands on a small pedestal in a dark robe, blessing with his right hand and holding an open book, while to his left stand Pope Mark in a red chasuble, the deacon Saint Agapitus and Saint Agnes, each on a footstool inscribed with a name. The tall, flat figures with their staring eyes show the solemn style of Roman mosaic in the 9th century. The full apse, commissioned by Pope Gregory IV, presents Christ as the Lord around whom the saints of the Roman church gather.
facts: The basilica was founded by Pope Mark in 336 and rebuilt by Pope Gregory IV, whose apse mosaic is the best-surviving part of his work.
The whole apse shows Christ between Pope Mark, Agapitus and Agnes on one side and Felicissimus, Gregory IV and Mark the Evangelist on the other, above a frieze of twelve lambs.
San Marco, beside Piazza Venezia, is today the national church of Venice in Rome.

commons:183258889.notes: This is San Marco in Rome, not St Mark's in Venice. Commons dates the mosaic 829–831; Wikipedia gives the rebuilding as 833 (Gregory IV reigned 827–844). Text in Christ's book was not read.
